To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the unilateral 6-OH-DA lesions of the DA neurons produced a well characterized functional asymmetry in mice, (2) the syngenic and the allogenic DA-rich cells grafted into the caudate nucleus of the mice with unilateral 6-O-DA lesions recovered the functional asymmetry, (3) the dopaminergic fibres grew predominantly into the ipsi- lateral caudate- putamen, and (4) the immunological responses in

the transplantation of syngenic DA rich cells of embryonic mesencephalon into the caudate nucleus of C57BL/ 6 (H- 2b) mice, with 6-OH-DA induced DA deficiency, produced the complete restoration of methamphetamine induced rotational response.

the intraperitoneal injection of methamphetamine induced a well-characterized asymmetry in the rotational behaviour of C57BL/ 6 (H- 2b) mice with unilateral lesions of the nigrostrial dopamine neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the damaged nigrostratal pathway in experimental animals with neurotoxic lesions of the dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra.
the reconstruction of the nigro-striatal pathway in experimental Parkinsonism by transplantation of syngenic or allogenic embryonic DA-rich cells.
the reconstruction of the nigro striatal dopaminergic pathway in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transplantation of embryonic ventricular mesencephalon cells into the caudate nucleus of the C57Bl/6 (H2b) mouse with 6-OH-DA lesions is an excellent model for studying the transplantation of embryonal cells into the brain of the Parkinsonian patient.
a syngenic or allogenic graft of embryonic mesencephalon can restore the function of a lesioned brain.
the DA-rich cells of syngenic or allogenic embryonic ventral midbrain are capable of integrating with the host tissue and restoring the function of the damaged nigrostrital dopamine pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transplantation of embryonic ventromesencephalic cells into the brain of mice with a unilateral 6-OH DA lesion produced a complete recovery of methampetamine-induced rotation.

the transplanted DA-rich cells from syngenic and embryonic allogenic mesencephalic tissues are capable of integrating and growing in the host brain, and that they can functionally restore the damaged nigrostratial dopaminergic system.
the transplants of syngenic or allogenic cells can restore a normal rotational response to methamphetamine in mice with unilateral 6-OH lesions of the DA neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single injection of embryonic DA-rich cells can produce a functional improvement in the behaviour of mice with unilateral lesions of the nigrostiatal dopaminergic pathway.
it is possible to reconstruct the nigrostriataI dopamine system by transplanting syngenic and/or allogenic embryonic cells into the brain of mice.

a complete functional recovery of the nigro-striatal dopaminergic pathway can be achieved by the transplantation of syngenic or allogenic DA-rich cells from the embryonic ventral midbrain into the caudate nucleus of the 6-OH-DA lesioned mouse brain.
